verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out in the tree. `Doc.mergeBlocks` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:379-389) issues `store.mergeBlock(...)` and then, whenever a flag is stranded, a second independent store write `store.applyStyles(edits)` via `dropStaleStyleOff` -> `writeStaleStyleOffEdits` (document.ts:481-485, 569-575). Under `YorkieDocStore`, `mergeBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2246, 2275) and `applyStyles` (1786, 1806) each open their own `doc.update()`, and `snapshot()` is a documented no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729), so there is no seam that folds them: two undo units for one Backspace. The diff's own comment at view/editor.ts:1049-1057 names this exact hazard, says folding needs a `batch()` seam on `DocStore` "that does not exist yet" (confirmed: no `batch` in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts) while the slides store has one (docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md exists), and defers it as a follow-up. `mergeBlocks` is reached from backspace/delete (text-editor.ts:1959, 2005, 2030, 2076) and from cross-block range deletes at the cited text-editor.ts:3243, 3345, 3411, so the deferred hazard is indeed extended from the rare style-redefinition path to the hot editing path. No guard makes the second write unreachable (the early return only fires when nothing is stale, i.e. the non-hazard case), and the concern is approach/sequencing fit against a prerequisite the repo's own design doc and this diff's comment establish, which sits in the design-fit lane. I also lack the originating issue's acceptance text, so I cannot rule the sweep's scope in or out; that uncertainty keeps the finding.

verdict.reason: The contradiction is real and present exactly as described. docs-font-controls.md:355-356 asserts "Both sweeps write through `DocStore.applyStyles`, so a redefinition stays one undo unit however many runs it strands." The `afterNamedStyleChange()` doc-comment at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1049-1057 states the opposite for the store used in collaboration: the cleanup is one unit but is "*not* folded into the redefinition" because `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op and the cleanup opens its own `doc.update()`, so "under the Yorkie store a redefinition that strands a flag takes two Cmd+Z, the first of which looks like it did nothing", pending a `DocStore.batch()` seam "that does not exist yet". Grepping docs/design/ for the caveat found it recorded nowhere in docs/design/docs/* (only the generic Yorkie one-update-one-unit mechanic in docs-intent-preserving-edits.md:112-121 and the slides seam in slides-native-undo.md:60-63), and docs-named-styles.md carries no undo statement for redefinition. So the canonical design doc states a user-visible undo guarantee the code deliberately does not provide, and the deferred seam is undocumented — a design-doc-discipline violation in this lens's lane, not a line-level logic bug.

finding.evidence: The diff folds `Doc.mergeCells`'s private copy into `normalizeInlines` on the explicit rationale that "a second copy here drifted from it and re-merged structural inlines". But `clipboard.ts:mergeInlines` (line 445) still merges any pair whose `inlineStylesEqual` agrees, with no `isStructuralInline` guard and no empty-run skip — the same drift, on the HTML-paste path that can carry two identical images. `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList` (`view/text-editor.ts:3816`) is a third copy, with its own hand-rolled equality `inlineStylesMatch` (3836) that compares a subset of keys — so clearing a key (the whole point of #749) can now make runs equal under one comparator and not the other. block-helpers.ts:87 even names that copy as the reference rule rather than reusing it.

verdict.reason: Presence verified. clipboard.ts:445 `mergeInlines` merges any pair whose `inlineStylesEqual` agrees, with no `isStructuralInline` guard and no empty-text skip, and is the merge rule for all HTML/markdown paste paths (calls at 434, 712, 719) — duplicating exported `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:89, guard at 96-98, empty-skip at 92). text-editor.ts:3816 `normalizeInlineList` is a third copy with its own comparator `inlineStylesMatch` (3836-3854) that omits `pageNumber`/`image` and compares colors with `===` where canonical `inlineStylesEqual` (types.ts:479-498) uses `storedColorsEqual`. block-helpers.ts:86-87 indeed names `TextEditor.normalizeInlineList` as the reference for the rule instead of that path reusing the helper, while document.ts:964-969 was folded onto `normalizeInlines` precisely because a second copy drifted. That is the duplication/incomplete-consolidation kind the design-fit rubric lists as major. Two sub-claims are weaker than stated but do not refute: clipboard.ts has no /pageNumber handling in its HTML walk (image styles only come from sanitizeInlineStyle at 130-163, which never calls mergeInlines), so the two-identical-images scenario is not presently reachable there; and for the boolean keys #749 covers, both comparators use `===`, so cleared-key divergence would not come from that key set (non-boolean keys are an explicit Non-goal, todo line 66).
